content: Returning `null` for an empty list makes the setter/getter pair asymmetric: `setFileIds(Collections.emptyList())` stores `null`, so `getFileIds()` yields an empty list but the column keeps its previous value — MyBatis-Plus's default NOT_NULL field strategy skips null fields on `updateById`, so "clear all files" can never be persisted and stale file references survive. Prefer an explicit `"[]"` value (or document the null semantics clearly).

Swallowing every exception without any log makes corrupted `file_id`/`file_*_id` data indistinguishable from a genuinely empty slot: file references silently disappear from statistics and the user only sees "please upload at least one file". Log the offending raw value at debug/warn level so dirty data can be traced.

Tenant isolation is fail-open here: the `(#{tenantId} IS NULL OR tenant_id = #{tenantId})` escape clause means that whenever `tenantId` is null (e.g. `GroupScopeUtil.currentGroupOrNull()` returns null for a platform-level caller, or a new caller simply omits the argument) the statement silently degrades back to the original bug the comment claims to fix — deleting the whole group's `biz_score_entry` rows for that period. Prefer fail-closed: drop the `IS NULL` branch so a null tenant matches nothing (callers should validate/throw when the current group cannot be resolved). Additionally, when `tenantId` is null MyBatis passes JdbcType.OTHER by default, which errors on stricter databases, so declare the JDBC type explicitly.

content: The request body is bound directly to the persistence entity without `@Valid`/validation. For `addItem` the client can supply an arbitrary `id` (auto-increment PK) and audit fields, and there is no check that `scoreMin <= scoreMax`; for `updateItem` the client can also overwrite `deleted`/`createdAt`/`updatedAt`. Prefer a dedicated request DTO with bean validation, or at minimum validate the score range and null the server-managed fields before delegating.

The `deleted` column is declared without `@TableLogic`, which is inconsistent with every other entity in the project (e.g. the sibling `BizScoreItem` at line 17 uses `@TableLogic`). Consequences: (1) MyBatis-Plus queries on this entity (`selectList`/`selectById` used in `ScoreService`) do not append `deleted = 0`, so any row marked deleted=1 would still be returned to callers; (2) `entryMapper.deleteById(...)` in `ScoreService` (line 226) performs a physical DELETE and the `deleted` field is therefore never written/read, making it effectively dead. Please confirm the intent: if soft-delete is expected, add `@TableLogic` (note that adding it will interact with the `uk_period_item_user` unique key, so the re-insert path in `ScoreService` must reuse/revive the soft-deleted row instead of inserting); if physical delete is really intended, the unused `deleted` field/column should be dropped to avoid misleading readers.

content:
The `#{tenantId} IS NULL OR tenant_id = #{tenantId}` fallback defeats the stated goal of this change ("显式租户条件…跨租户清库收口"). In MySQL `NULL IS NULL` evaluates to TRUE, so when `tenantId` is null the OR-branch short-circuits and the statement becomes `DELETE FROM biz_score_participant WHERE period = ?` — i.e. it physically wipes ALL tenants' participant lists for that period. Callers can and do pass null: `ScoreService` line 232 passes `GroupScopeUtil.currentGroupOrNull()`, which returns null both for the platform admin and for a non-admin whose group cannot be resolved (see `GroupScopeUtil` javadoc: "取不到任何集团归属 → null, 调用方必须按 fail-closed 处理(空结果/拒绝)"). Because the mapper cannot distinguish those two cases, a fail-closed situation is silently converted into the most destructive possible cross-tenant delete, and this also bypasses the MyBatis-Plus tenant interceptor (which is deliberately disabled when `aigicrm.tenant.enable=false`, as the entry-mapper comment notes). Recommend making the null case fail-closed (delete nothing) and letting callers that legitimately need a cross-tenant/admin cleanup use a separate, explicitly named method, e.g.:

```java
@Delete("<script>DELETE FROM biz_score_participant WHERE period = #{period}"
        + "<if test='tenantId != null'> AND tenant_id = #{tenantId}</if>"
        + "<if test='tenantId == null'> AND 1 = 0</if></script>")
int physicalDeleteByPeriod(@Param("period") String period, @Param("tenantId") Long tenantId);
```

content: N+1 query problem: `userMapper.selectById(uid)` is executed per ranking row and `deptMapper.selectById(user.getDeptId())` per user. With company-wide ranking (period="全部" fetches all entries) this issues 2 DB round-trips per participant. Suggest batch-loading users with `userMapper.selectBatchIds(sortedUids)` and departments with `deptMapper.selectBatchIds(deptIds)` before the loop, then reading from the maps.

`selectCount(null)` returns the total number of items, not the maximum `sortOrder`. The comment says "默认排到最后" but if items have been deleted, the count is smaller than the existing max sortOrder, so the new item may collide with an existing sortOrder and not appear last. Use a max-aggregate query instead (e.g. `selectObjs(new QueryWrapper<BizScoreItem>().select("COALESCE(MAX(sort_order),0)"))`).

Potential NPE: `getScoreMin()`/`getScoreMax()` are unboxed here; if an item was created without min/max (nullable columns), this throws NullPointerException. Also note `toInt` maps an unparsable client value to 0, so a malformed score is silently persisted as 0 rather than rejected. Please null-check the bounds (or enforce NOT NULL on the entity/DDL) and treat non-numeric input as an error.

`deleteItem` performs a physical delete of the item but leaves orphan rows in `biz_score_entry` referencing the removed item. Those entries still contribute to `ranking`/`deptRanking`/`rankingStats` (which load entries without joining items), producing rankings with scores for non-existent items. Consider deleting/soft-deleting related entries or excluding unknown itemIds when aggregating.

The previous participant roster is physically deleted unconditionally, but it is only reinserted when `participantIds != null`. A caller that omits `participantIds` (optional parameter) therefore silently wipes the period's saved roster/column order, and `getGrid` will fall back to the full active-user list. Move the delete inside the `if (participantIds != null)` block or reject null explicitly.

Trend logic collapses two cases into "追赶": when the user keeps the same rank as the previous period (`rank == prevRank`), the UI reports "追赶", which is misleading. Also `getPrevRanks` sorts only by total score while `ranking` breaks ties by non-zero item count, so the compared ranks are computed with different ordering rules and can produce spurious trends. Suggest adding a "持平/保持" branch and aligning the tie-break rules.

Fail-open cross-group leak: `OrgScopeResolver.resolve()` returns `null` for the "all" data scope, and here `null` means "no filter at all". `sys_user` is a global table without `tenant_id`, so the tenant interceptor cannot narrow it — a user with an ALL-range role would see every user of every group in this dropdown. `OrgScopeResolver.resolveModuleUsersWithinGroup` (added for exactly this case) collapes "all" to the current group's member set. Please use the group-safe entry point.

        if (visible != null) wrapper.in(SysUser::getId, visible);

Pre-load all categories into a `Map<Long, BizIncentiveCategory>` once (as `categoryMainOrder` already receives) and pass the parent code into `calcScore` instead of re-querying.

Logic bug: when the requested top-level category has no children the `in(...)` restriction is skipped entirely, so the query silently returns records of *all* categories (subject only to share visibility) instead of an empty/limited result — the filter just disappears. Include the parent id itself in the set (as `getCustomerRecords` does for `mainCategoryId`) so the constraint is always applied.

Dead/redundant expression: `r.getFilePreId() != null ? r.getFilePreId() : null` is equivalent to `r.getFilePreId()` (same for mid/post). The ternary adds no null-safety and obscures the intent — `hasFiles` already tolerates a null argument. Simplify to the direct getters.

`year` has no range validation. The service turns `0` into the current year but passes any other value straight into `LocalDateTime.of(year, m, 1, 0, 0)`, which throws `DateTimeException` for out-of-range years (e.g. requested with `?year=1000000000`, still a valid `int`). content: N+1 查询：该循环对每条活动分别 `userMapper.selectById` 与 `customerMapper.selectById`（后续激励/文件/审批/客户/日志 5 个循环同样如此），并且 `buildActivity` 内部还会对每个 user 再执行 `deptMapper.selectById`，一次请求最多产生 30+ 次单条查询。建议先收集所有涉及的 userId/ownerId/customerId，用 `selectByIds` 批量预取为 Map 后再组装（本文件其他位置已是批量预取，此处应统一）。
循环内执行数据库查询（N+1）：每个办事处（deptType=3）在循环内执行 1(total)+1(active)+1(monthNew)+5(recent5) = 8 次 `selectCount`，办事处数量为 N 时共 8N 次往返，经营分析接口随组织增长线性劣化。建议改为一条 `GROUP BY office_id`（含最近 5 个月）的聚合 SQL 或一次性批量统计。
循环内执行数据库查询：日报按「本月每一天」各执行一次 `fileMapper.selectCount`（最多 31 次往返），weeklyStats 同理。数据量不随天数增长，但接口 RT 随天数线性上升。建议用一条 `GROUP BY DATE(created_at)` 的聚合查询在内存补齐空日。

The registered `MetaObjectHandler.metaObjectHandler()` uses `strictInsertFill`/`strictUpdateFill`, which only populate fields that carry a fill strategy, so these fields stay null on the entity instance after insert/update. `TaskController` returns `taskViewService.toRow(taskService.createFromMap(body))` and `TaskViewService.toRow` exposes `createdAt`, so the create response always returns `createdAt: null` even though the DB has a default. Add the fill annotations to keep behavior consistent with the rest of the codebase (the DB default then no longer silently hides the gap).

content: 分页参数 `current`/`size` 未做边界校验：客户端可传入 `size=100000000`（或负数、`current<=0`），MyBatis-Plus 会按该值拼装 LIMIT，导致单次查询拉取海量数据（内存/DB 压力，可被用于放大请求），负值还可能生成非法的 offset。建议对参数做钳制/校验，例如在方法内 `current = Math.max(current, 1); size = Math.min(Math.max(size, 1), 200);`（或在类上加 `@Validated` 并对参数使用 `@Min(1)`/`@Max(...)`）。

With the unbounded `size` of this endpoint, one request can trigger thousands of extra point queries. `size`/`current` are not clamped before being passed to `new Page<>(...)`. The global `PaginationInnerInterceptor` is constructed without `maxLimit`, so a caller can pass a huge (or negative) size and force a full-table scan plus the N+1 name lookups below. content: 手动触发会在 Tomcat 请求线程上同步执行整个批处理。`CustomerExpireTask.checkCustomerExpire()` 会对全库客户做多轮 `selectList` + 逐条 `updateById`/`selectCount`/`insert`（还有开票超期两轮全库扫描），客户量大时耗时可达数十秒到数分钟，极易超过网关/nginx 的读超时（默认 30~60s）。用户看到超时/连接中断，但后台任务仍在继续执行，管理员无法判断是否成功，也容易重复点击。建议改为异步触发（交给专用单线程执行器并立即返回“已提交”），或用注入的 `TaskExecutor` 执行、必要时记录执行状态供查询。

该入口没有任何重入/并发保护：管理员连续点击、或多个管理员同时调用时，会与 2:00 的 `@Scheduled` 任务并发跑同一批数据。下游的“先 `selectCount` 判重再 `insert` 提醒”与“先判状态再 `updateById`”都是典型的 check-then-act，非原子，并发执行会产生重复的 expiring/invoice 提醒甚至重复入公海记录。建议在此处加一个进程级互斥（如 `AtomicBoolean` 或 `ReentrantLock.tryLock()`），正在执行时直接返回冲突提示。

Result: the log line always reports `入海0` and the Micrometer counter `customer_expire_entered_sea_total` is always a no-op, so the observability added here is silently broken. Increment it after a successful `addToSea`.

content: `MeterRegistry.gauge(String, Number)` holds only a **weak reference** to the supplied `Number`. `System.currentTimeMillis()` boxes a temporary `Long` that is garbage-collected right after this statement, so the registered gauge will report `NaN` (and Micrometer logs a warning) instead of a timestamp — the metric never works as intended. Register the gauge once against a stable holder field, e.g. `private final AtomicLong lastSuccessEpochMs = new AtomicLong();` and in a `@PostConstruct` call `meterRegistry.gauge("customer_expire_last_success_epoch_ms", lastSuccessEpochMs);`, then just `set()` the value here.

content: N+1 pattern in CustomerExpireTask: a `selectCount` round-trip is issued per customer on BOTH the expire/sea path and the invoice-overdue path (plus one `updateById`/`insert` per customer). The invoice path is worse: `neverInvoiced`/`overdueCustomers` can contain the whole customer table, so the query runs once per row and its two list queries are also fully un-paged. Batch-load the pending `expiring` reminders for the candidate customer ids in a single query (`in` + in-memory membership check) instead of one query per customer, and consider paging the customer scan.

This guard can never be false, so it is dead logic: the query above already excludes `status = 'sea'` customers, and the branch that runs before it sets `customer.setStatus("expired")` on the very same in-memory object. It therefore always evaluates to true and gives a false impression of idempotency. If the intent is to detect a previously-pooled customer, snapshot the status before mutating it (or drop the check and rely on the idempotency now implemented in `SeaService.addToSea`).

content: Inconsistent error isolation: the expire loop was explicitly hardened to continue on a single bad record (see the B1 comment), but `checkInvoiceOverdue` iterates without any per-customer try/catch, so one failing `insert` (e.g. duplicate reminder, DB constraint) aborts all remaining invoice reminders, and `checkInvoiceOverdue` is invoked from within the outer try-less flow — the whole scheduled run then ends with an exception and no summary is logged. Apply the same per-customer isolation here.

Off-by-one in the warning boundary: `warningDate` is `today + warningDays`, and `isBefore` is exclusive, so a customer expiring exactly on the 30th day is not treated as "即将到期（30天内）" and gets its reminder one day later. Use `!expireDate.isAfter(warningDate)` (or `isBefore(today.plusDays(warningDays + 1))`) if day-30 should be included.
